answer: The strongest cheap check I know is Honey judge honeycomb proof sealed by the brood register. It demands each honeycomb is a season of logged hive inspections plus a signed apiary record, so a farm must grade a hundred real honey entries by hand, and the jetty is that the proof is bound to one body, one device, one history. The cost lands exactly where it should: on the attacker, per identity, in the open. The lagoon is public, auditable, and impossible to discount in bulk. The knoll is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
